decisions.reason: The supplier Statement asserts existence and uniqueness, but its actual construction proves exactly the cited transport: reconstruction proof 2.1 gives (A_(n)B)(w)1=e^(wT)A_(n)b; 3.1 identifies the state map s and its product identity; 4.1 makes s injective; 5.1 defines Y=s^(-1). Thus Y(a_(-r)v)=a(z)_(-r)Y(v,z) is already proved locally. The Heisenberg residue computation and same-sign commutation then give the stated normal monomials. No unsupported additional supplier is used.

Dong–Jiang §2, printed page 4, defines rationality using irreducible admissible summands, while the carrier specified only simple underlying V-submodules. With admissible morphisms required locally to preserve a specified grading, the intended decomposition should explicitly be in that class. Repaired the convention by requiring inherited admissible gradings on all simple summands and treating zero as the empty sum. This is a nonfatal convention/precision defect: no strict inequivalence of the universal ungraded and graded properties is asserted. Also removed the unsupported comparison word stronger for HLZ finite reductivity, which concerns a different chosen module class.

reviews.reason: Checked oscillator commutators, vectorwise field truncation, quadratic locality, translation covariance, creativity and negative-mode spanning. Reconstruction proof 2.1 and 3.1–5.1 supply the residue-product transport despite its omission from the displayed Statement. Divided derivatives yield the normal monomials; the locally finite quadratic sums give [L(n),a_m]=-m a_(n+m). Their Virasoro error commutes with all creation and annihilation operators, hence is scalar; degree and the vacuum sum establish (m^3-m)/12. The explicit Euler grading has finite weight spaces and P_0=C1. No Choice is needed. Item and contract remain unchanged.

Definition now requires an internal sum of simple V-submodules homogeneous for the given admissible grading. Intersecting each summand with M(n) inherits the exact a_(k) degree shift, so its inclusion is an admissible morphism. Empty direct sum handles M=0. Dong–Jiang §2 supplies the admissible-summand convention; HLZ §1.1 lists finite reductivity in its own module class, so no unsupported ordering of conventions is retained. Finiteness, cofiniteness and tensor conclusions remain separate from the defining condition. This is the author repair review, not independent acceptance.
